task_title: documented bug-report and support intake path (issue template + support expectations)
task_criteria: FAILIF: .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE still has no template files, or CONTRIBUTING.md still offers only a bare issues URL with no reproduction template guidance and no stated support expectations/response intent. PROOF: find .github -maxdepth 3 -type f lists at least one ISSUE_TEMPLATE file, grep of CONTRIBUTING.md shows the support path and expectations section, and the documented links resolve (file existence plus the exact grep output pasted).

items.criterion: FAILIF: .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE still has no template files, or CONTRIBUTING.md still offers only a bare issues URL with no reproduction template guidance and no stated support expectations/response intent. PROOF: find .github -maxdepth 3 -type f lists at least one ISSUE_TEMPLATE file, grep of CONTRIBUTING.md shows the support path and expectations section, and the documented links resolve (file existence plus the exact grep output pasted).
items.detail: PROOF 1 — `find .github -maxdepth 3 -type f` (exit 0) prints: `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml`, `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — two ISSUE_TEMPLATE files exist. PROOF 2 — grep of CONTRIBUTING.md: `177:## Support and Bug Reports`, `180:with the [bug report form](.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml) (GitHub shows`, `183:is the difference between a report that can be reproduced and one that cannot be`, `203:What to expect: this is a small project maintained on a best-effort basis.`, `204:Issues are triaged when a maintainer is available; there is no guaranteed`, `205:response time and no support SLA.`, `211:- Open an issue: https://github.com/dexdat/SpecLang/issues`. CONTRIBUTING.md:182-198 is a reproduction checklist (version/commit, exact command + working directory, expected vs actual, output/error text, environment), so it is no longer a bare URL. PROOF 3 — documented links resolve: `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml` EXISTS, `SECURITY.md` EXISTS, `docs/NORTH_STAR.md` EXISTS, `README.md` EXISTS, `AGENTS.md` EXISTS. Commit 59b7b26f 'docs(contributing): add issue templates and support intake path (UX-004)' adds exactly these 3 files (+155 lines). Tests: `npx vitest run --passWithNoTests` -> `Test Files 1 failed | 112 passed | 4 skipped (117)` / `Tests 2 failed | 1947 passed | 58 skipped (2007)`; the 2 failures are tests/db.test.ts `SqliteError: attempt to write a readonly database` (pre-existing, unrelated to this docs-only change — db.test.ts passes 35/35 when run alone). [resolution 0.15; CONTRIBUTING.md]

items.criterion: The issue form is a valid GitHub issue-form schema (parses as YAML, has name/description/body, every body element has a supported type and unique id, and the reproduction fields the task requires are marked required) so GitHub will actually render it rather than reject it.

items.criterion: The support expectations stated in CONTRIBUTING.md and the issue form do not contradict each other or the repository's other support docs (SUPPORT.md / SECURITY.md), so a reporter is not given two different intake promises.
items.detail: CONTRIBUTING.md:203-207 ('best-effort basis ... triaged when a maintainer is available; there is no guaranteed response time and no support SLA') matches .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml:12-13 ('maintained on a best-effort basis: issues are triaged when a maintainer is available and there is no guaranteed response time'). Security reports are routed away from public issues consistently: CONTRIBUTING.md:200-201 -> SECURITY.md (file exists) and bug_report.yml:15-16 asks for secrets to be stripped. .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml:5-8 states Discussions is not enabled and links only the issue tracker, so the documented intake path is the one that exists. findings.detection: row marked status=complete while its own acceptance criterion is a board-state measurement that the same diff's edits could satisfy trivially, and the foreman_note admits NOT-A-FIX
findings.detail: QA-SPECLANG-4-R4 is flipped to "status":"complete" with foreman_note "NOT-A-FIX: this row's acceptance is a board-state measurement and it passes on the live board" — the row is closed without any change to the id-minter, so the underlying defect (duplicate id minting) is unaddressed and the row will not re-dispatch.

findings.detection: row marked status=complete while its own foreman_note states the fix is not proven and recurrence is expected
findings.detail: QA-SPECLANG-5-R5 is set to "status":"complete" with foreman_note "Not proof the minting convention is fixed; a recurrence is re-filed with a fresh measurement" — closing the row removes the only tracking item for the id-reuse defect.

findings.detection: completed row retains recovered:true / recovered_raw fields describing the pre-edit pending state, leaving contradictory status inside one record
findings.detail: QA-SPECLANG-5-R5 keeps "recovered_raw":"{\"status\":\"pending\",...}" alongside the new "status":"complete", so the record now contains two conflicting status values and any consumer reading recovered_raw sees pending.

findings.detection: completed_at/updated_at timestamp formats differ from the surrounding rows' convention
findings.detail: QA-SPECLANG-4-R4 uses "updated_at":"2026-11-17 10:36:19.000000" (space-separated, no timezone) while sibling rows in the same file use ISO-8601 with Z/offset (e.g. "2026-11-17T10:08:00.000000+00:00"), a format drift in the same field.

review.summary: The diff only mutates board bookkeeping: two QA rows are closed as complete on self-admitted NOT-A-FIX evidence, with one row retaining a contradictory recovered_raw pending status and a timestamp-format drift.
